newsitem.title: JAPAN: Compensation payments to widen Chisso 6-mth loss.
newsitem.headline: Compensation payments to widen Chisso 6-mth loss.

text.p: Chisso Corp said on Friday that it would post a larger net loss in the six months to September 30 than it originally expected due to compensation payments to victims of a mercury poisoning case.

The total compensation payments in the six-month period will total 16.6 billion yen, pushing the firm's half-year parent net loss to 19.60 billion yen from its original estimate of three billion yen, the company said in a statement.

Hundreds of people died and thousands were crippled in the 1950s and 1960s after eating seafood contaminated with organic mercury compounds dumped into Minamata Bay, 900 km southwest of Tokyo, by a plant owned by Chisso.
Last year, Japan's ruling coalition came up with a proposal to settle the 40-year-old dispute which included Chisso's compensation payments to victims.
